office_does: The three county commissioners set the county budget and property tax levies, make land-use and road decisions and oversee county departments.
race_blurb: First-term Commissioner Gunner Fulmer, a former firefighter-paramedic and police sergeant, faces business owner Troy Woody, who wants a public vote on a charter government with five part-time commissioners and a hired administrator. Both prefer the Republican Party; District 3 voters chose the finalists in August, and the whole county votes in November.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner since 2023 and incoming president of the Washington State Association of Counties, after nearly 30 years as a Walla Walla firefighter-paramedic and police officer.
highlights: Says he voted against seeking relief from the property tax cap: 'I do not believe higher taxes are the solution' [S3]
Wants the state to pay more of the cost of indigent defense, which he calls the top issue facing residents [S3]
Opposed a data center moratorium, saying the county cannot treat one business differently [S4]
Would keep speeding up permitting and work with legislators on state barriers to building [S2]
Will be sworn in as WSAC president in January 2027 if reelected [S1][S2]

experience.basis: First-term incumbent and former board chair who runs on his record and relationships, including a statewide counties' association leadership track.

taxes.basis: Reports voting 'No' on seeking relief from the property tax cap and repeatedly says higher taxes are not the answer to the deficit.

reform.basis: Stresses building relationships and working through existing institutions (WSAC, legislators, cities, the Port) to get results.

housing.basis: Wants faster, more predictable permitting and fewer state barriers that make it 'difficult and expensive' to build.

candidates.summary: Burbank business owner and former Columbia (Burbank) School Board member running to put charter-county reform to a public vote and pledging to serve at most two terms.
highlights: Would seek a charter-county vote: five part-time commissioners, a county administrator and appointed department heads [S1][S3]
Calls the deficit 'a structural problem, not a revenue problem' and proposes a zero-based budget review [S4]
Would extend permit-office hours and drop permits such as those for replacing windows [S3][S4]
Pledges a two-term maximum and a pay cut if reform passes [S1][S3]
The county Republican committee declined to endorse him over his charter platform [S2]

reform.basis: Core platform is structural reform: a charter-county vote that cuts elected offices and commissioner pay, plus a personal two-term limit.

experience.basis: Runs explicitly as an outsider ('I am not a politician') against entrenched incumbency, with only school board service in office.

spending.basis: Frames the deficit as overspending after 152% budget growth since 2008 and proposes a zero-based review of every department and contract plus salary cuts.

taxes.basis: Says the budget gap is 'not a revenue problem', implying cuts over new revenue, but makes no explicit tax pledge.

housing.basis: Would eliminate unnecessary permits, expand permit hours and online permits, and block new regulations without a public-safety justification.
